searchText: what default values do clients use for boost factor for p2p and builders? Prysm should default to zero boosts you mean `100` right? Yeah in the funny system the API uses it corresponds to 100 yeah, makes sense, we used the default of 90 that we had configured for mev-boost, but 100 makes more sense with epbs depends on the goal -- to avoid missing blocks due to others' fault, yeah, 100 is fine. to have control over what to include, less so I'm gonna be killing heze-devnet-1 in a few mins and spinning up heze-devnet-2 with beta.4 spec (12s slot). in order for letting people still iterate on shorter slots I think it would make sense to also launch heze-devnet-3 with 10 seconds slot. should we have two interop channels, fork n and n+1? its pretty quiet here but then I can silence the ones I'm not actively working on 🙂 so you would just silence both of them 😂 just H I'm still in G world actually I don't even know where I am atm, p2p folks keep inventing new things I can barely keep up https://dora.heze-devnet-2.ethpandaops.io https://notes.ethereum.org/@ethpandaops/heze-devnet-2 So shall I assume there's no consensus on that topic and we should be ready to have different building times per CL client for mainnet? My 2 cents are that a block's value that a CL client can build shouldn't be part of the equation when operators choose a client type. And given that past months the profit margins got quite thin, I'm afraid this can become (one of) the main drivers when making a choice. It seems that bid selection is a hot topic now and there's plenty of opnionated versions out there, I hope we could get to a sane defaults for all clients, but I don't have high hopes of that happening soon.
